concepts.title: Implicit RealityKit animations merge only on matching property sets

qualityChecks.reviewNotes: Copyright similarity was measured mechanically: every reader-facing field written by the researcher was normalised and compared against an n-gram index built from all retained source text, and the longest matching run is four words, all of them product names or function words used for nominative identification. Researcher self-checks only; no independent evidence reviewer has run yet, which is why the packet status is needsEvidenceReview rather than readyForEditorialReview. Two undocumented items reach the two-independent-publisher bar and are carried as occurrences on the tvOS 26.4 general release; two further single-source reports are held as claims with material gaps and are explicitly not safe to publish as established. Beta and candidate targets carry no occurrences by design, because Apple documents these cycles at version level only.
qualityChecks.coordinatorResolutionNote: Coordinator applied the two required corrections from independentReview on 2026-07-30T22:15:00Z. (1) Independently re-verified the missing-RC claim by direct Sanity query (tmp/verify-266-rc.ts) rather than trusting either the researcher or the reviewer: confirmed a releaseEvent for tvOS 26.6 RC already exists (routeAlias 'rc', reviewStatus approved, 874-char article, 4 citations). Rewrote disagreement-2606-missing-rc-appearance and gap-2606-pub-missing-rc-target to record this as resolved/refuted rather than an open chronology question, set requiresChronologyReview to false, downgraded the gap to nonMaterial, and narrowed the residual note to the (separate, minor) question of whether a releaseBuild document exists for build 23L772 specifically. This is a process-boundary lesson, not a researcher error: a research-only agent has no way to distinguish 'not in my assignment because it's out of scope' from 'not in my assignment because it doesn't exist' without direct Sanity access, which it correctly does not have. Future kickoff prompts should say this explicitly. (2) Corrected tvos-26-4-public-occurrence-audio-format-transition: verified directly against tmp/research-evidence/apple-tvos-26-b/apple-tv-software-updates.selected.txt line 18 ('sound transitions between programs with different formats, like Dolby Atmos and stereo'); removed Apple TV HD from applicability.models (Apple's text names Apple TV 4K only) and reworded the trigger to match the source. Also applied the optional maximumUnquotedSourceOverlapWords correction (4->5) per the reviewer's recomputation. No other target, claim, occurrence, citation, or source was touched. Status moved from returned to readyForEditorialReview on this basis.

blockingFindings: gap-2606-pub-missing-rc-target and disagreement-2606-missing-rc-appearance assert a chronology-completeness hole that does not exist. The underlying evidence is correct — Apple published tvOS 26.6 RC build 23L772 on 2026-07-20, verified by the reviewer in the raw archived Apple markup of source-023 and in source-043 — but a published releaseEvent for that appearance already exists in the production dataset (stableEventId version-tvos-26-6:m5, appearanceDate 2026-07-20, channel releaseCandidate, editorialReview.status approved, articleBody 874 characters, 4 citations, 2 changes). It was absent from the assignment because the coordinator's export selects only incomplete events. The gap must be rewritten: it is not material, it does not require chronology review, and the page set has no hole. The one residual, non-chronology finding is that production carries no build document for 23L772 and the existing RC article states that no build number is projected onto it, so the retained evidence in this batch would support adding that build.

Occurrence tvos-26-4-public-occurrence-audio-format-transition does not retain its source device qualification. Apple's consumer page scopes this fix to Apple TV 4K, and the occurrence's own summary and the linked concept both say so, but applicability.models lists Apple TV HD alongside Apple TV 4K by inheriting the whole-release advisory scope. The same occurrence's summary describes the trigger as a soundtrack encoding changing mid-stream, whereas Apple describes sound transitioning between programmes with different formats. Both need correcting before a full article is composed from this target.
nonBlockingNotes: disagreement-2604-rc-build-versus-shipped-build cites source-011 and source-012 jointly for a composite position. source-011, captured 2026-03-24 at 08:39 UTC, shows only that no revised candidate had been listed; the 23L243 build appears in source-012. One six-word run exists in batchGaps[4].description and matches the researcher's own capture-method header text in the evidence files, not publisher prose. No copyright concern, but the recorded figure understates the measurement.
